claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game continues to receive major, free updates featuring new maps, modes, and items over time.

citations.review_text: Game came out 8 years ago and they're still releasing major updates with new maps, modes, items, etc.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a variety of different challenges and special events to play.

citations.review_text:
BTD 6 is a great game to play with my friends, even though it is just four players that is enough for me to play with since not all of my friends own or play the game. It is also just a fun game to play through if you aren't sure what to play. Having the different challenges and events are great and fun and allow the game to still be fun even after you may complete all the difficulties.
I will say that over time, even with doing the events and doing different personal challenges, the game just gets to the point where it isn't as fun anymore because it's just repetition with not really any goal. I understand that there isn't supposed to be an end, but still. It's a great game to play for when you have free time but nothing to do in mind, and when you and your friends want to hang out online or in person together.
Fun game lots of different game play options to keep the intrest good chalanges

claims.claim: Reviewers complain about aggressive microtransactions, requests for payment for in-game currency or actions like restarting, and being charged money in a game that already has an upfront purchase price.

citations.review_text: Minus gazillion points for aggressive microtransactions and terrible netcode. The worst vices of cheap mobile games aimed at squeezing maximum money out of players.

I can see the appeal. It's a strategy game, litterally as the title says, monkeys defending something (idk the lore okay) from balloons. 
For me, personally, the game is far too fast paced. You get rewards every few seconds without even knowing what's going on and new monkeys before you even know how the ones you already have work.
My general critique is that you basically pay for a SUPERCELL mobile game (y'know the ones, those from Hayday and clash royale). Only, in those mobile games you have an addfree mobile game for free. This one forces you to pay for it and *still* keeps begging you for more money. 
Oh, you want to restart? Too bad, pay money for in-game currency.
Now, I would be fine if the game was free to play, but asking for money after I have already paid to own the game? That's ridiculous

Maybe in the future, when I feel like a fast paced dopamine addiction, I will give it another try, but for now I'll be giving up on it. 

Idk, maybe I'm autistic as hell but sensory overload much

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game receives frequent updates adding new content such as towers, maps, game modes, and events.

citations.review_text: I cannot recommend this enough for tower defense games. Constant fair balance patches, added base content, and dlc that are entire different games basically with the same towers. I mean the are on the 57th major update at the time of this review, each bringing a combination of new towers, maps, paragons, heroes, game modes, cosmetics, and more! If you haven't looked at this game in a while or are coming from playing earlier btd games you would be surprised at all the added content.

Fun game with plenty of stuff to do. The core tower defense gameplay is decently varied with new maps and towers being added regularly. The harder maps and difficulties certainly are a huge challenge. Beyond that, co-op, daily challenges and events (bosses, races, etc.) make this game have fantastic replayability.
